title: Berlin bear: fifteen-frame head-only roar
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: 15-frame transparent HEAD-ONLY replacement animation for an existing black woodcut Berlin bear.
Input reference: ONLY the head of the rightmost black heraldic bear in the attached image, never the bus or statue. Exact original bear character is mandatory. Preserve its original distinctive long squared left-facing snout, tiny unobtrusive eye, little rounded ears, open lower jaw and curling tongue, the nearly solid black woodcut/linocut ink silhouette. Head must not be redesigned as a teddy bear, grizzly photo, dog, cartoon, or smiling character.
Primary request: generate FIFTEEN sequential frames of that bear's HEAD AND SHORT UPPER NECK ONLY, doing a short bold ROAR. Omit the entire body, chest, arms, paws, legs, feet. The unchanged original body's pixels will be attached separately. Each neck ends in the SAME flat horizontal base, stable location and identical width, ready to overlap the original black neck seamlessly. Preserve source's very dark charcoal grain; no pale cheek scratch marks, no hair stripes, no shading, no glow.
Animation: head alone begins in original upright profile with long muzzle projecting left, mouth slightly open and tongue. Frame1 near original. Frames2–4 muzzle tilts up slightly and lower jaw hinges downward. Frames5–9 a clear powerful ROAR: jaw opens WIDELY, long upper snout pitches upward around12degrees, mouth gap creates an unmistakable bold transparent/cream negative space spanning a third of head height, only one or two restrained tiny carved teeth, dark tongue. No smiling, no angry cartoon eyebrows. Frames10–14 muzzle eases down and mouth closes to original. Frame15 near frame1. The jaw opening must be large and legible even when the entire full bear would display44pixels tall and this head is only14pixels tall. Move and open the muzzle, not the whole neck block. Head volume and identity consistent, small ears must remain.
Atlas layout: exactly5columns by3rows=15complete head/neck frames, row-major order. Prefer1536×1536 square canvas, fifteen equal cells. Each head uses same scale, identical neck anchor, same horizontal neck base and same head registration. Generous transparent padding/gutters around every head to contain open jaw and tilted muzzle. Each head and short neck should occupy about75%of cell width and60%of cell height. Do not change scale between poses. No labels, no numbers, no grid, no text.
Transparent alpha background including inside mouth negative space; no paper rectangles. Pure black/very dark charcoal woodcut ink with fine muted print grain, mature heraldic style. Not3D. HEADS ONLY: no arms, no paws, no shoulders, no body. Fixed flat neck base repeated at exact same position and width in all15cells.
notes: Generated PNG copied unchanged. Head-only roar with jaw opening and muzzle lifting; original body's source pixels should remain unchanged. The atlas is visually five columns by three rows, but unequal whitespace requires explicit crop rectangles, not fixed cells. Neck bases are horizontal. Align right edge and base of neck, preserving identical scale across poses. Source alpha>=128 yields bounds below; allow a little extraction padding for antialiasing.

original.integration: The erase polygon replaces head only while leaving raised paw intact. Original opaque neck crosses y256 around x1778..1938. Place generated neck base at y268 for about12px overlap. At1:1 source scale max roaring head height241 reaches y27, above original bear viewBox top87; allow overflow on animated SVG layer so roar is not clipped. Final packed overlay geometry should use actual pack anchor rather than stretching a square pack to these raw-source dimensions.
